summary: Intermittent 5xx errors traced to APIGW <-> VPC peering signal loss during tenant burst
description:
Issue summary: AtlasMaps reported a sudden elevation in 5xx responses for production tenant during a traffic hotspot. Impact: Many short-lived requests receiving 502/504 and aborted streaming sessions, customer reports degraded UX in map tile generation and conversational assistants. Environment: Dedicated tenant on us-west cluster using private VPC peering into Redwood Private nodes.

Observed symptoms:
- APIGW returning 502/504 to clients with upstream error messages referencing 'connection reset' and 'no route'.
- Upstream serving runtimes intermittently logged sudden full-worker disconnects and process restarts around the same timestamps.
- Burst began ~2026-03-10 03:18:00 UTC and recurred in 5–10 minute waves for ~90 minutes.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Simulate tenant burst by replaying customer traffic pattern (tile generation + streaming chat) against the dedicated tenant in prod-us-west.
2) Monitor APIGW metrics (upstream_5xx, conn_resets), VPC peering tunnel metrics (rx/tx errors, mtu drops), and runtime health endpoints.
3) Observe whether APIGW begins to signal upstream disconnects under the same traffic pattern.

Expected: Stable <1% 5xx under burst with graceful retries and streaming continuations.

Impact statement: Customer-visible errors affecting product usage; billing unaffected but SLA risk due to error rate spike.

Attachments: sample logs, metric graphs, and pcap snippets uploaded to the ticket attachments area.
comments: 2026-03-10 03:34 - Maya Thompson (Support): Customer reported ~18% of requests returned 5xx over a ~90 minute window. Requested immediate triage and potential failover to fallback region.

2026-03-10 03:46 - Ravi Gupta (SRE): Starting initial triage. Observed concurrent small spike in VPC peering interface errors and APIGW upstream resets. Opening network-level traces and notifying infra networking team via #support-net.

2026-03-10 04:05 - Elena Cruz (Oncall Serving): Correlated with a sharp increase in KV cache misses for this tenant which amplified request volume to backends. Not seeing memory OOMs on serving nodes, but connection churn is high.

2026-03-10 05:12 - Maya Thompson (Support): Customer confirmed error window aligned with a scheduled internal traffic spike from their side. They requested temporary routing to eu-central as a mitigation if possible.

2026-03-11 09:00 - Ravi Gupta (SRE): Applied short-term mitigation: increased APIGW upstream keepalive timeouts and enabled fallback routing to a warmed standby pool for the tenant. Monitoring for recurrence.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis A: VPC peering tunnel experienced transient packet drops/high retransmits leading to TCP RSTs between APIGW and private serving proxies. Evidence: CloudVPC metrics show 2–3x retransmit rate spike concurrent with 5xx waves.
Hypothesis B: Tenant-level KV cache miss storm amplified backend fanout and saturated connection pools on private serving proxies, triggering connection queue timeouts and upstream failure responses.
Logs: Upstream proxy logs show repeated 'upstream connection reset by peer' and 'connection timed out while reading response headers' within the same minute where APIGW 5xx increased.
Tracing: Distributed traces show request spans failing during the backend init phase (before model generation) — suggests failure occurs at proxy/connectivity layer, not model computation.

Repro: Replayed customer burst in a staging mirror with controlled VPC peering error injection recreated 502 surge within expected window. Confirms sensitivity to packet loss under prefetch-heavy bursts.

Temporary mitigations tested: 1) Increase socket backlog and keepalive on APIGW; 2) Throttle prefetch concurrency at tenant proxy; 3) Route tenant to warmed standby pool. All reduced error rate to <2% under same traffic shape in lab.

Planned long-term fix: Implement adaptive prefetch gating (cap concurrent prefetch per tenant during detected peering degradation), harden VPC peering MTU negotiation, and improve APIGW upstream retry/backoff logic to avoid cascading retries.

Follow-ups assigned: Networking (Anita Verma) to validate peering fabric health and cloud provider tickets; Serving (Jin Park) to instrument prefetch counters and add tenant-specific gating; Platform (Ravi) to rollback default keepalive changes if side-effects observed.

resolution: Mitigation applied: APIGW upstream keepalive increased, tenant warm-standby routing enabled, and prefetch concurrency limited for the tenant. Networking opened a cloud provider support ticket and replaced the peering endpoint. Error rate returned to baseline <1% after actions.
resolution_notes:
Short-term: keepalive and standby routing deployed 2026-03-10 08:15 UTC; prefetch gate rolled to staging and limited to 6 concurrent prefetches for tenant at 2026-03-10 10:00 UTC.

Long-term: Networking to finalize peering endpoint swap and validate MTU/path MTU stability. Serving team to add tenant prefetch throttles and APIGW will receive backoff tuning to reduce retry amplification.

Customer communication: Maya provided mitigation summary and ETA for peering replacement to AtlasMaps. Customer accepted standby routing and will report if they observe further issues.

Post-incident follow-up: Schedule postmortem and update runbook regarding 'detect and throttle prefetch on peering degradation' (Owner: Jin Park).
